paragraph: Raxio Group runs data centres in Angola. In December 2025 its chief technology officer said [Raxio builds medium-voltage lines direct from the substation to each of its facilities](<https://african.business/2025/12/technology-information/inside-the-race-to-fire-up-africas-power-hungry-data-centres>). He said it [always uses two power lines, each able to carry the load, plus diesel generators](<https://african.business/2025/12/technology-information/inside-the-race-to-fire-up-africas-power-hungry-data-centres>). No earlier position has been found, so no change is recorded in the last twelve months. No PUE and no water figure has been found for a data centre in Angola. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[CIO Mag reports that Benin's data centres run on dual power feeds from the national utility SBEE, plus standby generators](<https://cio-mag.com/datacenters-et-energie-lequation-de-la-transformation-numerique/>). That puts a data centre on a secured supply. No source found says power is set aside for data centres. No power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.6 or less has been found for any data centre in service, nor a figure for water use or cooling that uses no water. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

Raxio's CIV1 data centre in Abidjan opened in September 2024. Its chief technology officer says [it is fed by two independent 15kV feeders direct from the CIE substation](<https://africanreview.com/ict/powering-the-civ1-data-centre-in-cote-d-ivoire>). In the last twelve months, in December 2025, he said [Raxio always uses two such lines, plus diesel generators](<https://african.business/2025/12/technology-information/inside-the-race-to-fire-up-africas-power-hungry-data-centres>), in every market. That repeats the design and does not change it. No PUE and no water figure has been found for a data centre in Cote d'Ivoire. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

ST Digital's Douala01 data centre has [two utility feeds, one power transformer and three backup generator sets](<https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-ready-v1-site-assessment-v1-0-rev1-2-st-digital-douala01-pdf>). The operator gives these figures, and a design and yearly PUE both under 1.5, in its 2024 OCP Ready self-assessment. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives a water figure, or says power is set aside for data centres. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

Raxio Group runs data centres in DR Congo. In December 2025 its chief technology officer said [Raxio builds medium-voltage lines direct from the substation to each of its facilities](<https://african.business/2025/12/technology-information/inside-the-race-to-fire-up-africas-power-hungry-data-centres>). He said it [always uses two power lines, each able to carry the load, plus diesel generators](<https://african.business/2025/12/technology-information/inside-the-race-to-fire-up-africas-power-hungry-data-centres>). No earlier position has been found, so no change is recorded in the last twelve months. No PUE and no water figure has been found for a data centre in DR Congo. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

On 27 October 2026 the regulator ARPCE said [nationwide power cuts and scarce diesel were badly disrupting data centres](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/crise-du-carburant-les-reseaux-telecoms-bout-de-souffle-172163>). In the last twelve months, on 22 September 2026, the government said [works on the national data centre stood at 82%](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-infrastructures-le-data-center-operationnelle-dici-fin-2026/>). The 12 MW Kintelé solar farm [is being built to keep its power stable](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-infrastructures-le-data-center-operationnelle-dici-fin-2026/>) and is not yet in service. No data centre in service has been found with two grid feeds, its own substation or line, or its own power plant. Preparing would need a data centre in service with a secured power supply.

[Le Jeune Indépendant says Algeria's Centre national des services numériques is connected to several energy sources](<https://www.jeune-independant.net/centre-national-des-services-numeriques-lalgerie-scelle-le-virage-vers-leconomie-2-0/>), beyond its batteries and standby generators, with fully redundant power. That puts a data centre on a secured supply. No source found says power is set aside for data centres. No power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.6 or less has been found for any data centre in service, nor a figure for water use or cooling that uses no water. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Raxio's data sheet says the ET1 data centre in Addis Ababa takes a 33kV utility supply directly fed from the nearest substation, with 2N power redundancy and 72 hours of on-site fuel](<https://www.raxiogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/RAX016-4-Data-Sheet-SITE-ET1-v2.pdf>). The sheet also states a PUE of 1.3, and Ethio telecom gives its Gola Sefer modular data center a PUE of 1.4. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No water use has been found. None is on record for any data centre in service in Ethiopia. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Officials said a photovoltaic power plant provides nearly 22% of the energy of Gabon's sovereign data centre, inaugurated by the president, which also runs on a 15kV main line with N+1 backup units](<https://itweb.africa/article/gabon-launches-sovereign-data-centre/xnklOvz14JDq4Ymz>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No PUE of 1.6 or less has been found. No water use has been found. No cooling that uses no water has been found in Gabon. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Onix Data Centres says its Accra facility takes power from its own 2,200-panel solar farm by day and the grid at night](<https://onixdatacentres.com/home/infrastructure/>), with three 456 kW generators as backup. Module 1 is fully operational, and the solar farm peaks at 640 kW. That puts a data centre on a secured supply. No source found says power is set aside for data centres. No power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.6 or less has been found for any data centre in service, nor a figure for water use or cooling that uses no water. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

On 12 February 2026 KenGen's chief executive said [the Olkaria green energy park now lets data centres take power direct from the generator](<https://www.the254report.co.ke/p/kengen-extraordinary-general-meeting-egm>), and the regulator EPRA has pre-cleared it. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, plans for the [Microsoft-G42 data centre at Olkaria stalled over available power](<https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/24/can-kenyas-ai-ambitions-coexist-with-naivashas-water-needs>), Al Jazeera reports. [IXAfrica's NBOX1 campus on Mombasa Road runs at a PUE of 1.25](<https://cioafrica.co/tcs-sovereign-cloud-goes-live-in-nairobi/>), the company says. The newest water statement is from 2022. It is too old to count. Mature would need a data centre in service to publish its water use, or state that its cooling uses no water, from the past three years.

No stage is set. [Atlas Cloud Services states a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.5, with free cooling, for its Benguerir data centre](<https://atlascloudservices.com/en/our-data-center/>). No source found says a data centre in service in Morocco has two grid feeds, its own substation or line, or its own power plant. None from the past three years says one went short of power or water. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a data centre in service with a secured power supply: two grid feeds, its own substation or line, or its own power plant.

[Raxio's own specification page says the MZ1 data centre in Matola takes a 15 kV utility supply fed directly from the nearest substation](<https://www.raxiogroup.com/data-centres/mozambique/>). The page gives N+N redundancy and 48 hours of on-site fuel, and states a PUE of 1.3 with indirect adiabatic cooling. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No water use has been found. None is on record for any data centre in service in Mozambique. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Mordor Intelligence says Mauritius Telecom's live Tier IV data centre has N+2 architecture and two independent utility feeds](<https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/mauritius-data-center-market>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No PUE of 1.6 or less has been found. No water use has been found. No cooling that uses no water has been found in Mauritius. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Kasi Cloud Datacenters commissioned its Lekki campus in Lagos on 19 May 2026](<https://nsia.com.ng/kasi-cloud-datacenters-commissions-west-africas-first-hyperscaleready-ai-capable-data-centre-campus-in-lagos/>). In the last twelve months, the campus has listed [a direct 132kV connection to the Transmission Company of Nigeria](<https://nsia.com.ng/kasi-cloud-datacenters-commissions-west-africas-first-hyperscaleready-ai-capable-data-centre-campus-in-lagos/>) and hybrid gas, solar and battery supply. No earlier dated position has been found. No source found gives a Nigerian data centre's water use. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[Lomé Data Centre says it has a 2N electrical architecture with dual utility feeds from the national grid, with automatic transfer, plus diesel rotary UPS and fuel for several days](<https://lomedatacentre.tg/en/infrastructure>). Its home page states a PUE of 1.4. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No water use has been found. None is on record for any data centre in service in Togo. Establishing would need power set aside for data centres: a signed supply contract, a plant built for them, or a tariff or zone in force.

[CPT1 in Cape Town takes wheeled solar power under an agreement signed in March 2023](<https://www.africadatacentres.com/africa-data-centres-announces-additional-6mw-capacity-now-live-in-cape-town/>). [Teraco's CEO reported an average yearly PUE of 1.43 for 2025](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/sa-data-centre-operators-push-back-amid-sustainability-probe/5yONP7EroNQMXWrb>), and [Teraco gives its water use as 0.04 litres per kWh in 2024, down from 0.10 in 2023](<https://www.teraco.co.za/blog/water-scarcity-in-africa/>). Both figures are Teraco's own. In the last twelve months, [Teraco says the first wind power from its own producer reached its Cape Town data centres in September 2026](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/teraco-brings-wind-power-into-sa-data-centre-mix/mQwkoq6YrAnM3r9A>).
